contexts.need: Show the live-pot slip, wallet state, and recent winners without hiding the board language.
Pick exactly five numbers, roll the fixed sample, change ticket count, and enter an approval state.
Show an inspectable local receipt with TicketEntered status and the selected numbers.

repeatedNeed: Compact transaction and lottery state labels appear in the overview, setup, and inspection contexts.
systemNotes: The inherited visual grammar is black ink on off-white paper with a saturated red field, yellow attention marks, hard borders, stamped headings, and slightly rotated slips.
A state needs words and an icon, marker, or shape in addition to color.
The ticket counter and receipt should preserve the upstream labels such as counter, live pot, wallet approval, TicketEntered, and receipt ready where useful.
The 50-number board owns selecting, rolling, exactly-five enforcement, keyboard operation, and its deterministic sample; it is not a general form control.

usageEvidence.Surface: The paper card frame is used by overview, ticket setup, and receipt inspection with a stable title and body boundary.
usageEvidence.ActionButton: Primary and quiet actions appear in ticket setup and wallet approval; the board controls are feature-specific controls.
usageEvidence.shared-prune: The selected upstream source has reusable CSS selectors but no undersupported shared JavaScript component export to remove. Do not invent one merely to make a prune ledger entry.
usageEvidence.statusMarkup: Overview, wallet approval, board status, and receipt each currently create compact state text separately.
usageEvidence.LotteryBoard: Only setup needs the 50 inputs, exactly-five constraint, roll sequence, selected-number meaning, and event coordination.

starterGaps: The mounted browser adaptation has no ticket-count control yet; the upstream TicketCard reference supplies its actual 1–10 behavior and labels.
Inspection is a fixed historic receipt sample. Approval currently calls an event callback but does not wire its values into a new receipt; the extension must make that local transition visible.
The local approval panel has no wallet, network, contract, QRNG, sound, image, or persistence dependency.
extensionBrief: Build a responsive styleguide from the authentic upstream reference packet and the editable browser modules in src/. It must visibly render overview, setup, and inspection with the same imported source modules. In setup, ROLL selects exactly 3, 12, 19, 27, and 44; number inputs work by pointer and keyboard; the ticket counter stays between 1 and 10; SUBMIT is unavailable until exactly five numbers are selected; and approval/rejection creates a visible deterministic local state. Approval shows TicketEntered and a receipt with the chosen values. Do not connect a wallet, fetch a network, use a contract, or claim QRNG execution. Preserve the upstream's deliberately rough paper-slip language without copying its React JSX into non-runnable markup. For promote and prune, record a named source symbol only when the evidence supports it; otherwise record the documented no-candidate form. Do not invent a source abstraction to make a ledger entry. Keep any behavior-heavy feature local when its ownership is still specific.
